newsitem.title: USA: Harrah's says union-backed proposal fails.
newsitem.headline: Harrah's says union-backed proposal fails.

text.p: Harrah's Entertainment Inc said Friday afternoon that preliminary voting results indicate that a shareholder proposal to amend its by-laws to redeem the company's shareholder rights plan and require approval by a majority shareholder vote for adoption of any such shareholder rights plans in the future failed to pass.

The company said that contrary to a statement issued earlier Friday by the Hotel Employees and Restaurant Employees International Union, which conducted a proxy solicitation in support of the shareholder proposal, the proposal, which requires the approval of 75 percent of outstanding shares, apparently did not even receive the vote of a majority of outstanding shares.

The union said previously that it feels that the 75 percent vote requirement is an illegal restriction on shareholders' statutory powers to amend the bylaws, and that the issue may have to be settled through litigation.
Harrah's said final results of the shareholder vote will be contained in the company's 10-Q, which will be filed by May 15.
